title: Crave Connect
description: A Zomato-style food app with an intelligent recommendation system. A friend and I both worked on the backend before we dropped it.
longDescription: Crave Connect was meant to be a Zomato-style food app with an intelligent food recommendation system. A friend and I both worked on its backend before we dropped the project. The backend is a FastAPI service over PostgreSQL with 19 tables covering restaurants, menus, orders, delivery, payments and reviews. Menu items get pgvector embeddings, and a plain-language query is resolved with Google's generative AI and LangChain into a ranked list of dishes.

chapters.title: The idea
chapters.body: A food app in the style of Zomato, with an intelligent way to recommend what to eat.

chapters.title: What we built
chapters.body: The backend. A FastAPI service over a PostgreSQL database of 19 tables: restaurants, menus, orders, delivery, payments, reviews and more.

chapters.title: The smart part
chapters.body: Every menu item gets an embedding stored with pgvector. A craving typed in plain words is turned into a search over those embeddings, and the best matches come back as recommendations.

chapters.title: What happened
chapters.body: My friend and I both worked on the backend. We dropped the project. The last commit is from August 2025.

title: MUJ Placement Portal
description: Our college's placement office, the team that helps students get hired, tracked placements by hand. A friend and I built them one portal on a central database: he built the backend, I built the screens the staff work in. Our juniors run it today.
longDescription: Placement software for the Training and Placement office at Manipal University Jaipur, built with a friend. I built the staff dashboards, student profile pages and the screens that show each person what their role allows; he built the backend, the database and the bulk importer. Prototype in June 2025, rebuilt from scratch in 2026, used by roughly 80 to 100 staff (our estimate) and now run by our juniors.

chapters.title: The problem
chapters.body: Our college's Training and Placement office, which helps students get hired, tracked placements by hand.

chapters.title: The request
chapters.body: They asked a friend and me for one portal, with all their data in one central database on the university intranet.

chapters.title: Who built what
chapters.body: My friend built the backend, the database and the bulk importer. I built what the staff see: dashboards, student profiles, and screens that show each person only what their role allows.

chapters.title: Who uses it
chapters.body: The placement team, heads of department and senior staff, each seeing what their role allows. Students never log in.

chapters.title: What arrived
chapters.body: Moving the manual records in brought inconsistent fields, duplicate students and failed bulk uploads.

chapters.title: Patch or rebuild
chapters.body: Our first version went live in 2025 and we kept maintaining it, but new features meant changing code we already struggled with. So in January 2026 we rebuilt it from scratch, in three months.

chapters.title: The handover
chapters.body: Our juniors joined two months into the rebuild and built parts of it with us. We handed it over in walkthroughs, and they run it today.

chapters.title: Next time
chapters.body: Check data as it's imported, not after it lands. Write the docs while building. And add automated tests: we had few.

credits.what: Staff dashboards and tables, student profile pages, role-based views, sign-in screens
Backend and REST API, the PostgreSQL database, the bulk importer
Parts of the rebuild, from two months in; they maintain it now

title: Stock Analysis System
description: An experiment with Google's Agent Development Kit: five agents that answer plain-English questions about a stock. Built solo.
longDescription: An experiment with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK), built solo. You ask about a stock in plain English, like "Why did Tesla stock drop today?", and five agents identify the ticker, fetch the price and the news, work out the price change and analyse it with Google Gemini. Data comes from Finnhub, Alpha Vantage, Twelve Data, Marketaux and Yahoo Finance, and the system falls back to another source when one fails or hits its rate limit. It runs as a FastAPI service and plugs into the ADK web interface.

chapters.title: The experiment
chapters.body: This was my experiment with Google's new Agent Development Kit (ADK), built on my own. It runs as a FastAPI service and also plugs into the ADK web interface.

chapters.title: Five agents
chapters.body: Each agent does one job: identify the ticker, get the price, gather the news, work out the price change, and analyse it all with Google Gemini.

chapters.title: The data
chapters.body: Finnhub, Alpha Vantage, Twelve Data, Marketaux and Yahoo Finance. If one source fails or hits its rate limit, the system tries another.

chapters.title: Ask it anything
chapters.body: You ask in plain English, for example: Why did Tesla stock drop today?

title: Eye Gaze Tracking
description: Real-time eye gaze estimation that can move your cursor. My minor project, built by a team of 3 and trained on the GazeCapture dataset.
longDescription: A real-time eye gaze tracking system. MediaPipe finds the face and the eyes, and a hybrid deep-learning model reads the face, both eyes, the head pose and some metadata (ResNet50 for the face, EfficientNetB3 for the eyes) to estimate where you are looking. It was trained on the GazeCapture dataset, reaches 80%+ accuracy at 30 FPS with a 5.3° mean error, and can move the mouse cursor from your gaze. A team of 3 built it as our minor project, and I did most of the work.

chapters.title: What it does
chapters.body: It watches a face through a camera in real time and works out where the person is looking. It can even move the mouse cursor to that spot.

chapters.title: How it works
chapters.body: MediaPipe finds the face and the eyes. A hybrid model then reads the face, both eyes, the head pose and some metadata: ResNet50 looks at the face and EfficientNetB3 looks at the eyes.

chapters.title: The results
chapters.body: It was trained on the GazeCapture dataset. It reaches 80%+ accuracy at 30 FPS, with a mean error of 5.3°.

chapters.title: Where it came from
chapters.body: It was our minor project in the third year of college. We were a team of 3 and I did most of the work.

title: EcoHive
description: A green credit trading platform for a sustainable future, built around trees, water, air and mangroves. My first project, made by a team of 5 for SAP Hackfest 2024.
longDescription: EcoHive is a green credit trading platform. Its mission is planting trees, conserving water, purifying the air and nurturing mangroves. Individuals and organisations sign up, see a live credit balance and send credits to each other. A team of 5 built it for SAP India's Hackfest 2024, where it reached the Top 50 out of 2000+ entries nationwide. It is live on the web.

chapters.title: The idea
chapters.body: EcoHive is built on green credit. Its mission is planting trees, conserving water, purifying the air and nurturing mangroves. The platform is where green credit can be held and traded.

chapters.title: What you can do
chapters.body: Individuals and organisations each sign up, see a live credit balance, and send credits to each other by email.

chapters.title: How it went
chapters.body: It was my first project. I built it with a team of 5 for SAP Hackfest 2024, in my second year. It reached the Top 50 out of 2000+ entries nationwide.
